sections.skill: Calculate income tax with marginal brackets and compare marginal and effective rates

questions.prompt:
For this scenario, use these hypothetical single-filer brackets: 10% on taxable income up to $12,000; 12% on income from $12,000 to $48,000; 22% on income from $48,000 to $100,000.
Under a bracket system like this, what rate applies to the FIRST $12,000 of everyone's taxable income?

choices.text: The person's highest bracket rate

questions.intro: Federal income tax uses marginal brackets: income is taxed in layers. Each layer of income is taxed at its own rate. Moving into a higher bracket raises the rate only on the dollars in that bracket, not on all your income.
questions.feedback: Every filer's first $12,000 is taxed at 10% under these brackets.

misconceptions.A: Thinks one rate applies to all income

sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt:
For this scenario, use these hypothetical single-filer brackets: 10% on taxable income up to $12,000; 12% on income from $12,000 to $48,000; 22% on income from $48,000 to $100,000.
Omar's taxable income is $40,000. What is his federal income tax?
questions.intro: To compute tax with brackets: tax each layer of income at its rate, then add the layers.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Omar's taxable income is $40,000 and his tax is $4,560. What is his EFFECTIVE tax rate?
questions.intro: The marginal rate is the rate on your last (next) dollar of income. The effective (average) rate is total tax ÷ income × 100, which is lower than the marginal rate because lower layers are taxed less.

misconceptions.A: Divides income by tax and misplaces the decimal

sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt:
For this scenario, use these hypothetical single-filer brackets: 10% on taxable income up to $12,000; 12% on income from $12,000 to $48,000; 22% on income from $48,000 to $100,000.
Leo's taxable income is $60,000. He gets a $1,000 raise. How much more federal income tax does he owe?
questions.intro: A raise is taxed at the marginal rate of the bracket it falls in. Moving further into a bracket never makes total take-home pay go down from income tax alone.
questions.feedback: The extra $1,000 is in the 22% bracket: $1,000 × 0.22 = $220.

misconceptions.D: Re-taxes all income at 22% plus more

sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Which statement about marginal tax brackets is TRUE?

choices.text: Entering a higher bracket raises the tax rate on all of a person's income
Everyone pays the same rate on all income
Only the income inside a higher bracket is taxed at the higher rate
Brackets apply only to people over 65

questions.correct_answer: Only the income inside a higher bracket is taxed at the higher rate
questions.feedback: Higher rates apply only to the dollars in the higher bracket.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

sections.relationship: Bracket tax works like tiered pricing: each tier is charged its own rate.

questions.prompt: A water bill charges $2 per unit for the first 10 units and $3 per unit after that. What is the bill for 14 units?
questions.intro: Tiered pricing charges different rates for different layers. Income tax brackets work the same way.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Using 10% on the first $12,000 and 12% above it, how much income is in the 12% layer for taxable income of $20,000?
questions.intro: Income in a bracket = total income − the bottom of that bracket (up to the bracket's top).
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: What is 12% of $8,000?
questions.intro: Tax on a layer = income in the layer × rate.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Using 10% on the first $12,000 and 12% above it, what is the total tax on $20,000?
questions.intro: Total tax = tax on each layer, added together.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: What is a "marginal" rate?

choices.text: The rate on the next dollar earned
The average rate paid across the whole income
The lowest rate in the system
A rate set by the taxpayer

questions.correct_answer: The rate on the next dollar earned
questions.feedback: Marginal = the rate on the last or next dollar.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: A person earns $55,000 of wages and has $40,000 of taxable income. Their tax is $4,560. What share of their WAGES goes to federal income tax (nearest tenth)?
questions.intro: Tax as a share of total income is lower still than the effective rate on taxable income, because deductions shield part of income.

questions.prompt: Which rate should be used to estimate the tax on extra income from a side job?

choices.text: The effective rate
The rate for the lowest bracket
The marginal rate
Zero, because side income is not taxed

questions.intro: The marginal rate is the rate on the next dollar of income. The effective rate is total tax ÷ total income, an average across all brackets. Extra income is stacked on top of what you already earn.
questions.feedback: Additional income is taxed at the marginal rate.

misconceptions.D: Believes small side income is untaxed

sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Rosa turns down extra shifts, saying, "If I earn more I'll be in a higher bracket and take home less." Under marginal brackets, what is TRUE?

choices.text: She is right; all her income would be taxed more
She keeps most of each extra dollar; only that income is taxed at the higher rate
She would owe more tax than she earns
Extra income is never taxed

questions.correct_answer: She keeps most of each extra dollar; only that income is taxed at the higher rate
questions.intro: Under marginal brackets, earning more always increases after-income-tax pay, because only the extra income is taxed at the higher rate.
questions.feedback: Extra income is taxed at the marginal rate, leaving most of it for her.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Rosa earns $1,000 more, taxed at 22% income tax and 7.65% FICA. How much of the $1,000 does she keep?
questions.intro: Extra wages face both income tax at the marginal rate and FICA (7.65%).
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: Which situation CAN reduce a person's benefits when income rises?

choices.text: Losing eligibility for some income-based credits or aid
Tax brackets themselves
FICA taxes
Sales tax

questions.correct_answer: Losing eligibility for some income-based credits or aid
questions.intro: Some benefits shrink as income rises (phase-outs), which can feel like a higher tax, but brackets alone never reduce take-home pay.
questions.feedback: Phase-outs of credits or aid can matter; brackets alone do not reduce take-home pay.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: A person moves from $47,000 to $49,000 of taxable income, crossing into the 22% bracket at $48,000 (this scenario). How much of the extra $2,000 is taxed at 22%?
questions.intro: Only the dollars above the bracket threshold are taxed at the higher rate.
questions.feedback: Only the $1,000 above $48,000 is taxed at 22%; the other $1,000 is taxed at 12%.
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)

questions.prompt: For that $2,000 increase (from $47,000 to $49,000, crossing $48,000), how much more tax is owed?
questions.intro: Tax on the extra income = (amount in the lower bracket × its rate) + (amount in the higher bracket × its rate).
sources: IRS (Federal income tax rates and brackets): Federal income tax uses progressive marginal brackets; thresholds change yearly. This course uses stated hypothetical brackets. (https://www.irs.gov/filing/federal-income-tax-rates-and-brackets)
